transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I’ve started eating big amounts by myself at night because I’m embarrassed for anyone to see how much I’m eating. It's just been really hard to admit, but my primary doctor suggested I should talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to get rid of the food by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Oh, no, I don't do any of those things, doctor. I've never made myself throw up, taken laxatives, or tried to fast or exercise it off. Usually, I just sit there on the couch late at night feeling so heavy and ashamed of myself.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen, and has this pattern been going on for at least 3 months?

Yes, doctor, it's been happening at least once or twice a week for about five months now. It really started back then when my daughter and my youngest grandbaby moved out of state and the evenings got so quiet.
Did these eating episodes begin after a major loss or separation, such as a bereavement, divorce, or a child moving away, and do they feel tied to that event?

Yes, doctor, it's absolutely tied to that. It started about five months ago, shortly after my daughter and youngest grandbaby moved out of state and my daily childcare routine just vanished. The house got so quiet, and I feel like I've just been using food to try and fill that empty space and the loneliness I feel without them.
Do you feel the eating started mainly as a response to the stress or sadness from your daughter and grandbaby moving away, and does it improve when you feel less lonely or more supported?

Yes, it definitely started as a reaction to the sadness of them moving away and leaving my house so quiet. But because I've been hiding this and turning down invitations to church, I haven't really had a chance to feel supported or less lonely lately. I'm not sure if that would make it improve, but I know the loneliness is what drives me to do it.
Since your daughter and grandbaby moved away, have you also been feeling persistently sad or unable to enjoy things most days, or is the main problem mainly the eating episodes when you feel lonely?

I miss my daughter and grandbaby terribly and the quiet evenings are lonely, but I wouldn't say I feel a constant, persistent sadness or that I can't enjoy anything anymore. The main, overwhelming struggle is definitely these eating episodes and the deep shame and guilt I feel right after. I've only been turning down church events lately because I'm so embarrassed about my eating habits, not because I don't want to see my friends.
Since your daughter and grandbaby moved away, have you had persistent low mood or loss of interest in most things nearly every day, or is the main issue mainly the eating episodes and loneliness?

The main issue is definitely the eating episodes and the loneliness, rather than a constant loss of interest in everything. I still enjoy working on my quilts, watching the Saints games, and doing my PTA work. It's just when the evenings get quiet that the loneliness hits and the eating starts, leaving me feeling deeply ashamed afterward.
Have these eating episodes and the related distress lasted less than 6 months since your daughter and grandbaby moved away, or have they been going on longer than that?

Yes, they've been going on for about five months now, so it has been less than six months. They moved away about seven months ago, and it took a couple of months of the house being so quiet before I started eating like this.
Have the eating episodes and the distress around them stopped getting better, or are they still continuing now even as you adjust to your daughter and grandbaby being away?

Yes, doctor, they are definitely still continuing and haven't gotten any better at all. It has been a very consistent pattern for about five months now, happening at least once or twice a week. The deep feelings of shame and that awful sense of being unable to stop myself haven't eased up even as time has passed.
Have the eating episodes and the distress around them lasted less than 6 months since your daughter and grandbaby moved away, or have they been going on longer than that?

Like I mentioned, it's been going on for about five months now, so it has been less than six months. My daughter and grandbaby moved away about seven months ago, and this eating pattern started a couple of months after they left once the loneliness really set in.
Have these eating episodes and the distress around them been improving at all as you adjust, or are they still clearly ongoing and causing problems most days?

They are definitely still ongoing and haven't improved at all over these past five months, happening at least once or twice a week. It's causing real problems for me because I've started turning down church potlucks and dinner invitations out of embarrassment and fear that I'll overeat. Instead, I just end up staying home alone with my food.
